_doc: Cherry MX switches and keycaps. Cherry publishes the keycap's slot; no official spec exists for the switch stem, so stem sizes are measured by the community. kind as in x1c.json, plus estimate: a reasoned guess nothing confirms yet. Measure it, then make it measured.
name: mx

slot.rule: Keycap cross slot is 4.1 (+0.05) mm across

slot_arm.rule: Keycap cross slot arms are 1.17 ± 0.02 mm wide

stem.rule: Switch stem cross is about 4 × 4 mm

post.rule: Round post around the keycap's slot, as on most MX keycaps

slot_depth.rule: Depth of the cross slot in the post

cap_base.rule: 1u keycap width at the bottom: leaves about 0.85 mm between neighbours

stem_arm_h.rule: Switch stem's horizontal cross arm: 1.25 to 1.30 mm thick (middle of the range)

stem_arm_v.rule: Switch stem's vertical cross arm: 1.05 to 1.10 mm thick (middle of the range)

stem_height.rule: Switch stem stands about 3.7 mm above its slider

height_pcb.rule: Switch top (stem) is 15.2 mm above the PCB, with no keycap

housing.rule: Top housing width where it sits on the plate

housing_top.rule: Top housing width at its top surface (it tapers): not found in any source
housing_top.source: Estimate: measure a switch with calipers

below_plate.rule: Switch and its pins reach this far below the plate's top: a case under a handwired plate must clear it
below_plate.source: https://adamws.github.io/3d-printed-keyboard-prototype-with-freecad/ ("anything above 8.5 mm should cover switch pins")

relief.rule: Opening under the 1.5 mm clip layer of a thicker plate, so the switch's latches can spring out: nobody publishes a size
relief.source: Estimate: thick plates are undercut to 1.5 mm (https://www.keebtalk.com/t/fat-plates/2787); test that a switch clicks in

pcb_pin1_x.rule: PCB footprint: pin 1, right of the switch's centre (seen from above, the back of the board up)
pcb_pin1_x.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_pin1_y.rule: PCB footprint: pin 1, behind the switch's centre
pcb_pin1_y.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_pin2_x.rule: PCB footprint: pin 2, left of the centre
pcb_pin2_x.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_pin2_y.rule: PCB footprint: pin 2, behind the centre
pcb_pin2_y.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_pin_drill.rule: PCB footprint: drill for the two electrical pins
pcb_pin_drill.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_pin_pad.rule: PCB footprint: copper pad around each electrical pin
pcb_pin_pad.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_centre_hole.rule: PCB footprint: unplated hole for the switch's centre post
pcb_centre_hole.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_peg_x.rule: PCB footprint: the two fixing pegs (PCB-mount switches), either side of the centre
pcb_peg_x.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_peg_hole.rule: PCB footprint: unplated holes for the fixing pegs
pcb_peg_hole.source: KiCad footprint library, Button_Switch_Keyboard.pretty/SW_Cherry_MX_1.00u_PCB.kicad_mod (from Cherry's MX catalogue, http://cherryamericas.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/mx_cat.pdf), https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-footprints

pcb_body.rule: The switch's bottom housing sits on the PCB in this square: nothing taller than a pad goes under it on the top side
